correctness.rationale: Kirchhoff determinant on the feasible connected-support domain has strict logdet concavity since individual edge weights inject into grounded Laplacian; the optimum saturates budget, and torus translations force uniform positive weights by uniqueness. Fourier eigenvalues yield the finite matrix-tree product, while strict Cauchy–Schwarz proves D_n/A_n monotone with full range, giving a unique exact root and reciprocal symmetry. Summing over one Fourier direction with the exact cyclic Poisson resolvent gives F_n(u/n²)=nH(u)−1+O(n^-1) with one derivative uniformly on compact u. Monotone inversion yields u_kappa and positive v_kappa; small/large-u expansions establish 1/(nQ) finite-price and 4/(pi²Q²) infinite-volume power laws. Independent cofactors and finite resolvent checks corroborate only small n.

value.rationale: The price-driven collapse of one lattice direction is a natural singular design limit; the complete unrestricted optimization and noncommuting price/volume limits, with explicit first-order correction, are useful quantitative network-design results rather than a rederivation of the known toroidal spanning-tree determinant.

final_claim: For n≥3 square torus C_n×C_n, nonnegative independent conductances and directional cost ratio Q>0, weighted spanning-tree enumerator has a unique unrestricted optimizer with two positive homogeneous directional weights. The ratio t=b/a solves D_n/A_n=Q uniquely; if Q=kappa n, t=u_kappa/n²+v_kappa/n³+O_kappa(n^-4) with u from H(u)/u=kappa, positive v, and sharp opposite limit power laws.
limitations: Only simple square tori n≥3 and two direction-wise linear costs; fixed kappa asymptotic not uniform in kappa extremes; no rectangular or higher-dimensional cases.
residual_risks: A specialist weighted-spanning-tree/asymptotic lattice free-energy paper may have the price-dependent resolvent asymptotic under different variables; fixed-anisotropy related full text not exhaustively inspected.
